about.title: San Jacinto Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Jacinto's mix of local streets and busier corridors like Ramona Expressway and San Jacinto Avenue sees a steady flow of traffic, and public records show 162 injury collisions and 228 injured people in the most recent final year on file. Wednesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. show up more often in crash timing than other windows, which lines up with commuters and school-related traffic converging on the same stretches of road. Whatever road you were on when it happened, the aftermath tends to look the same: medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster calling faster than you'd like. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise results — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney working on contingency who can look at what happened, explain your options under California law, and help you avoid early mistakes that could hurt your claim later.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a public road authority — is involved. Waiting too long to get advice can quietly cost you your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You Fast
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces what you can collect. An early recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to inflate your share of fault before you've even seen a police report.

items.title: No Cap Means Documentation Matters More
items.desc: California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but that only helps if the evidence supporting your claim is preserved — skid marks, dashcam footage, and witness statements can disappear within days of a crash on roads like Ramona Expressway.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's usually best to avoid recorded statements to the other side's insurer until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to shift fault or minimize your injuries. An independent attorney can help you understand what, if anything, you're required to say.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in San Jacinto?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, such as one responsible for maintaining Ramona Expressway or State Street, played a role in the crash, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months. Because these timelines vary by situation, it's worth getting a claim reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover damages even if you share some responsibility for the crash. Your total recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. An independent attorney can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.
